subject: religious-studies
title: Life After Death: Foundations
welcome_lead: Today you'll meet the key vocabulary for life after death in Christianity and Islam.
meta_desc: GCSE RS Life After Death foundations — soul, heaven, hell, judgement, resurrection.
final_note: You now know the foundational beliefs about death and what follows.

concepts.def: Spiritual part of a person believed to survive death
God deciding the eternal fate of each person

walkthroughs.body_html:
Christians believe that after death there is judgement, then either heaven or hell.

Resurrection of the body, not just immortality of soul, is the Christian hope (1 Corinthians 15).

Jesus' resurrection on Easter is the foundation: 'Because I live, you also will live' (John 14:19).

Muslims believe in Akhirah — the afterlife.

At death, angels take the soul. There is a period of waiting (Barzakh) until Yawm al-Qiyamah (Day of Resurrection).

On that day everyone is judged: deeds are weighed (Qur'an 21:47) and the soul is sent to Jannah (Paradise) or Jahannam (Hell).

Christian images of heaven: Revelation 21 describes 'a new heaven and a new earth' with 'no more death. or pain'.

Islamic Jannah: gardens beneath which rivers flow (Qur'an 13:35).

Both faiths use vivid imagery while teaching the deepest reality is relationship with God.

mcqs.q: Which Arabic word names the Islamic afterlife?
In which Bible chapter does Paul give his classic teaching on resurrection?
What do Christians mean by resurrection, and how does it differ from reincarnation?
options: Resurrection and reincarnation are basically the same idea of life after death.
Jesus was a human who became God after his resurrection.
Christians believe everyone is reincarnated until they accept Jesus.

Resurrection is the once-for-all bodily raising to eternal life at the end of time (modelled on Christ's resurrection); reincarnation is the soul's repeated rebirth into new bodies. They are distinct doctrines from different religious traditions.

mcqs.q: What do orthodox Christians believe about the nature of Jesus?
options: Jihad is the Islamic word for prayer.
He is fully God and fully human at the same time (the incarnation) — both natures united in one person, as defined at the Council of Chalcedon.
Jesus was a human who became God after his resurrection.
Jesus was half God and half human.

mcqs.q: What does the term jihad mean in Islam?
options: Jesus was a human who became God after his resurrection.
Struggle or striving — the greater jihad is the internal spiritual struggle against sin; the lesser jihad refers to defensive military struggle under strict conditions.
Jihad is the Islamic word for prayer.
